perspective:
Gloria Bangura’s available information:

- She knows she is an administrative assistant at a large event planning company, and Donald Ortega is a part-time bartender at company events. They are professional colleagues who mainly interact during events and are not personally close.
- Over several company events, she directly observed Donald seeming distracted, low-energy, and less enthusiastic while serving drinks.
- She initiated a conversation with Donald and asked if everything was okay with his job. He told her he was “not as into it as I used to be” and that it was “kind of repetitive.”
- After reflecting on that conversation, she suspected his job dissatisfaction might point to deeper personal issues. She suggested he consider talking to a professional. Donald said he hadn’t considered it and wasn’t sure it would help.
- Following that conversation, she sensed a shift in Donald’s behavior toward her and worried he might resent her suggestion as overstepping. She apologized to him and explained she only meant well. Donald told her he was “a bit taken aback at first” but understood she meant well, and said it was “a lot to process.”
- She felt relieved that the tension seemed to ease, and she invited Donald to collaborate on a new project, saying it could use his creative input. Donald accepted and said it sounded like a great opportunity.
- After working with him on the project, she observed Donald’s strong contributions and renewed enthusiasm. She concluded he was a valuable team member and publicly acknowledged his work during a meeting. Donald thanked her, said it meant a lot to him, and expressed that he felt appreciated.
